Hi Maria,

Great to meet you on last week's call — excited to get the POC started. To make the kickoff productive I want to align on two things up front: scheduling and capacity expectations so we can prep the right environment (Hosted trial vs Dedicated reserved capacity).

Proposed next steps:
- 45–90 minute POC kickoff + hands-on working session (prompt review, routing config, short load smoke test).
- Short follow-up capacity planning touch to size quota bumps / token budgets if needed.

Options for kickoff (ET):
- Tue, Mar 2, 10:00–11:30
- Thu, Mar 4, 15:00–16:30

Quick questions to help us prepare:
1) Expected peak QPS for the POC load tests (ballpark).
2) Average prompt + response token length we should assume (avg and max).
3) Any compliance or VPC requirements that would force Private/Dedicated vs Hosted.

I attached a short POC playbook and an example prompt set to speed things up. If those dates don't work, happy to propose a couple alternatives — just let me know who from your side will be attending (platform/engineering + product are ideal).

Thanks,
Rishi

Subject: Re: FinTechX POC trial onboarding & capacity alignment

Heads-up on capacity strategy for the March 7 working session — my notes: 

- FinTechX target for POC load test: 25 QPS peak (avg ~10–12 QPS). Avg token size ~400, spike to 1,200 for rare requests.
- Recommendation: start with Hosted trial + quota bump for the 2-week POC window. Hosted gives fastest turnaround and we can raise rate limits and token quotas immediately.
- Load test plan: ramp in three stages (1 QPS -> 10 QPS -> 25 QPS) over 30 minutes, monitor tail latency and KV cache behavior. Capture token-level cost trace for analysis.
- Dedicated only if they want sustained >100 QPS or need VPC/on-prem security. For short high-throughput bursts we can do a short Dedicated reservation but procurement will need a simple short-term contract (estimate lead time 3–5 business days to provision).

Attachments: capacity_calc.xlsx (simple worksheet with cost estimates for Hosted quota-bump vs 2-week Dedicated reservation).

Connor — can you produce a rough cost/time estimate for a 2-week dedicated reservation (N GPUs, provisioning time) so I can include that in the reply to Maria? I can own the load test harness and prompt review artifacts.

-Marissa
Senior Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Summary of action items and notes:
- FinTechX: confirm final QPS target and token budget by Wed, Mar 3.
- Redwood: submit Hosted quota-bump request (pending numbers) and produce 1-page SLA + billing cadence for Procurement (Rishi).
- Marissa: prepare prompt review deck and load test harness; will run the three-stage ramp during the working session.

Quick answers to Procurement questions (preliminary):
- Hosted rate limits: default tenant rate-limits are enforced per-API-key; standard windows are per-second and per-minute tiers. For POC we can configure a tenant-scoped quota that raises both the per-second and per-minute thresholds; exact numbers depend on requested QPS.
- Dedicated provisioning: Redwood handles provisioning and we provide the IP allowlist guidance; customers typically provide the final list. Lead time for short reservations is typically 3–5 business days after signed agreement.

Attachments: redwood_poc_playbook.pdf, example_prompt_set.csv, capacity_calc.xlsx

Looking forward — I'll follow up with the SLA doc and Connor's estimate by Fri EOD.
